# LMR (LabSync LIMS) — Institutional Repository Blueprint & Agent Guide

> **Important**: This document is the single source of truth for all AI agents working on this codebase. Read this document before inspecting code or writing changes to avoid re-investigating the architecture from scratch.

---

## 1. Project Goal & Institutional Context

### Primary Persona & Purpose
- **User Role**: Lab In-Charge at an academic institution in Nepal (Secondary / Higher Secondary / College levels — Class 11, Class 12, and undergraduate labs).
- **Core Mission**: Modernize laboratory operations by replacing paper logbooks, manual registers, and scattered Excel sheets with a clean, high-clarity institutional digital system (**LabSync LIMS / LMR**).
- **Dual Core Responsibilities**:
  1. **Academic Practical Operations**: Class 11 & 12 batch schedules (e.g. Science A/B), practical experiment syllabi, roll-call attendance tally, faculty session logging, and dual sign-off (Teacher + Lab In-Charge).
  2. **Laboratory Infrastructure & Maintenance**: Routine preventive care and servicing for Computer Labs (BIOS updates, thermal paste, deep PC cleaning, software/OS installation, cable management) as well as Physics, Chemistry, and Biology laboratories (equipment inspection, glassware check, calibration).

---

## 2. Technical Stack & Architecture

- **Framework**: Next.js 16+ (App Router) with React 19, React Server Components (RSC), and Server Actions in `app/actions/`.
- **Language**: TypeScript (strict mode enabled). Every task **must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` with 0 errors**.
- **Styling & UI**:
  - Tailwind CSS with custom CSS variables (`app/globals.css`).
  - Dark / Light theme support with system toggle. Canvas: Deep Obsidian (`#0B0F19` dark; rich midnight slate surfaces `#101726`, elevated wells `#151E32`) and Pearl Slate (`#F8FAFC` light).
  - Modern Typography Stack:
    - Heading: `Plus Jakarta Sans` (`--font-heading`, `font-heading`).
    - Body/Interface: `Inter` (`--font-sans`, `font-sans`).
    - Bilingual Devanagari Fallback: `Noto Sans Devanagari` (`--font-devanagari`) baked into `--font-heading` and `--font-sans` font families for clean Bikram Sambat rendering.
    - Code/Monospace: `JetBrains Mono` (`--font-mono`, `font-mono`).
  - Radix UI primitives (`@radix-ui/react-*`), Lucide React icons (`lucide-react`).
  - High-performance layered surface `.glass-card` and `.glass-header` (eliminates GPU lag).
  - Global `tabular-nums` for numeric and financial/attendance alignment.
- **Database & Backend**:
  - Supabase PostgreSQL with Direct Connection Pool (`lib/db.ts`).
  - Typed schema models in `types/database.ts`.
  - Database access via `@supabase/supabase-js`, `pg` Pool (`getPgPool`), and server clients in `lib/supabase/server.ts`.
- **Calendar & Dual-Date System**:
  - Gregorian (AD) dates integrated with Bikram Sambat (BS) Nepali calendar (`nepali-date-converter`, `lib/nepali-calendar.ts`, `components/admin/dual-calendar-picker.tsx`).
- **Export & Reporting Engines**:
  - ExcelJS (`lib/exports/xlsx.ts`) for styled `.xlsx` workbooks with official NEB 3-tier signature blocks.
  - CSV export (`lib/exports/csv.ts`).
  - High-fidelity A4 landscape print sheets (`app/(dashboard)/print/*`) with `@media print` shields.

---

## 3. Database Models & Schema Summary

### `profiles`
- Institutional accounts: `id`, `full_name`, `email`, `role`, `approval_status`, `permissions` (JSON), `created_at`.
- Roles: `'super_admin' | 'lab_incharge' | 'hod' | 'teacher'`.
- Statuses: `'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected'`.
- Note: Legacy `department` has been eliminated from the data model and user profiles. Use **Role Badge & Assigned Lab / Facility Scope**.

### `labs`
- Physical and virtual laboratory facilities.
- Fields: `id`, `name`, `code`, `capacity`, `type` (`computer_lab`, `physics_lab`, `chemistry_lab`, `biology_lab`), `status` (`'Operational' | 'Under Maintenance' | 'Inactive'`), `is_active` (`boolean`), `created_at`.
- Database constraint: `CHECK (status IN ('Operational', 'Under Maintenance', 'Inactive'))`.
- Active lifecycle rule: `is_active` is automatically derived (`status === 'Operational'`).

### `academic_years`
- Institutional operational cycles.
- Fields: `id` (e.g. `'2083'`), `name` (e.g. `'2083/84'`), `start_date`, `end_date`, `is_current` (`boolean`), `created_at`.

### `classes`
- Academic grade and stream definitions.
- Fields: `id` (e.g. `'11sci'`, `'12eng'`), `name`, `grade_level` (11 or 12), `stream`, `is_active`, `created_at`.

### `class_subjects`
- Curricular subject mapping per class.
- Fields: `id`, `class_id`, `subject_code`, `subject_name`, `weekly_quota`, `created_at`.

### `students`
- Student biographical records.
- Fields: `id` (UUID), `admission_no`, `registration_no`, `full_name`, `gender`, `is_active`, `archived_at`, `archive_reason`, `created_at`.

### `student_enrollments`
- Academic year cohort enrollment linking students to classes.
- Fields: `id`, `academic_year_id`, `class_id`, `student_id`, `roll_number`, `section`, `status`, `created_at`.
- Constraint: `CHECK (status IN ('active', 'transferred', 'graduated', 'archived', 'completed'))`.

### `workstations`
- Physical laboratory desks and computing nodes.
- Fields: `id`, `lab_id`, `label` (e.g. `'PC-01'`), `pos_x`, `pos_y`, `device_type` (`pc`, `mac`, `server`), `row_label`, `is_active`, `created_at`.
- **Operational Status Invariant**: Operational status is NOT a static column. It is dynamically derived from `workstation_issues` (`in_progress` &rarr; `under_repair`, `open` &rarr; `flagged`, else &rarr; `operational`).

### `floor_elements`
- Architectural floor components for CAD rendering.
- Fields: `id`, `lab_id`, `element_type` (`door`, `window`, `pillar`, `board`, `podium`, `bench`), `label`, `pos_x`, `pos_y`, `width`, `height`, `rotation`.

### `workstation_seat_plans`
- Student-to-workstation assignments per class & academic year.
- Fields: `id`, `lab_id`, `academic_year_id`, `class_id`, `workstation_id`, `enrollment_id`, `notes`, `assigned_by`, `created_at`.

### `workstation_issues`
- Hardware and software fault tickets.
- Fields: `id`, `workstation_id`, `reported_by`, `title`, `description`, `severity` (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`), `status` (`open`, `in_progress`, `resolved`), `resolved_at`, `created_at`.

### `practical_logs`
- Completed or skipped practical sessions logged by instructors.
- Fields: `id`, `schedule_id`, `lab_id`, `teacher_id`, `date`, `period_label`, `subject_name`, `batch_group`, `practical_title`, `total_students`, `present_students`, `absent_students`, `absent_rolls`, `remarks`, `status`, `skip_reason`, `topic_learned`, `logged_by`, `created_at`, `academic_year_id`, `class_subject_id`.
- Note: Verification is stored in `remarks` (e.g., verified stamp) or `logged_by`.

### `schedules`
- Weekly institutional timetable.
- Fields: `id`, `day_of_week` (0=Sunday to 5=Friday), `time_slot`, `slot_id`, `span`, `lab_id`, `teacher_id`, `subject_code`, `subject_title`, `class_grade`, `default_students`, `status`, `created_at`.

### `maintenance_plans`
- Preventive maintenance routine definitions.
- Fields: `id`, `title`, `description`, `lab_id`, `cadence` (`daily`, `weekly`, `biweekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semester`, `yearly`), `checklist` (`string[]`), `affected_machines` (`string[]`, e.g. `['PC-01', 'PC-02', ...]`), `category`, `is_active`, `created_by`.

### `maintenance_logs`
- Historical certified service logbook entries.
- Fields: `id`, `plan_id`, `lab_id`, `performed_by`, `performed_at`, `asset_identifier`, `work_performed`, `observations`, `next_recommended_date`, `status`, `created_at`.

### `lab_incidents`
- Equipment breakage and hazard register.
- Fields: `id`, `title`, `lab_id`, `reported_by`, `equipment_name`, `incident_type`, `severity` (`minor`, `moderate`, `major_critical`), `status` (`reported`, `investigating`, `resolved`, `escalated_to_hod`), `resolution_notes`, `resolved_at`.

### `audit_ledger`
- Immutable audit log tracking sensitive changes.
- Fields: `id`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `action`, `actor_id`, `before_state` (JSONB), `after_state` (JSONB), `metadata` (JSONB), `created_at`.

---

## 4. Roles & Permissions Architecture (`lib/permissions.ts`)

| Role | Access Level | Primary Focus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Super Admin** (`super_admin`) | Full root access | User approvals, role assignment, system reset, timetable configuration, maintenance routines, cohort promotion. |
| **Lab Incharge** (`lab_incharge`) | Laboratory operations | Maintenance Workbench (`/maintenance`), CAD floor plan, workstation triage, attendance verification, routine execution. |
| **Head of Dept** (`hod`) | Department oversight | Incident escalations, syllabus progress review, departmental practical audits, board compliance. |
| **Teacher** (`teacher`) | Instructor access | 1-click practical logging (`/logs/new`), Live Lab Cockpit roll-call, viewing timetable, reporting broken equipment. |

---

## 5. Development History & Key Milestones Completed

### A. Academic Practical Logbook & Routine
- Built interactive session logging (`/logs/new`) with Class 11/12 roll attendance counter and auto-calculated attendance percentage.
- Implemented dual-signoff tracking (Subject Teacher log entry + Lab In-Charge digital audit verification).
- Formatted A4 landscape printable registers (`/print/records`, `/print/daily-log`) and Excel exports.

### B. Timetable Engine & Live Lab Pods
- Interactive Weekly Routine Grid (`/schedules`) supporting Sunday–Friday academic schedules.
- Live Lab Pods on the main dashboard (`/`) displaying real-time occupancy, current ongoing subject, instructor name, and quick session logging.

### C. Incident & Damage Escalation System (`/incidents`)
- Breakage and fault triage workflow with severity levels and HOD escalation triggers.
- Printable incident damage register (`/print/incidents`).

### D. Lab Maintenance Workbench (`/maintenance`)
- Streamlined 2-tab Workbench: Routine Tasks & Schedules vs. Certified Service History Logbook.
- Embedded Admin Console (`/admin` Tab 03 &rarr; Maintenance Routines) with 1-click presets.
- Zero pricing/cost clutter: focus strictly on technical upkeep and academic safety.

### E. Design System & Modern Typography Overhaul
- Brand Typography: Plus Jakarta Sans (`font-heading`), Inter (`font-sans`), and JetBrains Mono (`font-mono`).
- Bilingual Devanagari Integration: Loaded `Noto_Sans_Devanagari` with explicit weights `['400', '500', '600', '700']` and `subsets: ['devanagari']` attached via `--font-devanagari`.
- UI Primitives: High-density `.glass-card` surfaces without GPU-taxing repeated backdrop-blur.

### F. Phase 6: Unified Master Blueprint — Workstation Cockpit Elevation & Institutional Intelligence
- **Track 1: CAD Workstation Floor & Live Cockpit Elevation**:
  - Interactive Viewport (`hooks/use-canvas-viewport.ts`): Clamped zoom ($0.5\times$ to $1.6\times$) with cursor-centered focal scaling, multi-touch pinch, middle-click/space-drag panning, and workstation auto-centering beacon.
  - Floating HUD Controls (`components/computer-lab/canvas-controls-hud.tsx`): 1-tap zoom, fit-to-screen, 1:1 reset, pan mode toggle, and minimap toggle (strictly zero literal `+` labels).
  - Radar Minimap (`components/computer-lab/canvas-minimap-radar.tsx`): 34-node live floor preview with interactive draggable/clickable bounding viewport box.
  - Living LCD Workstation Nodes (`components/maintenance/workstations/workstation-node.tsx`): Chamfered milled bezels, status LEDs, glowing attendance rings, and tactile spring click response.
  - High-Speed Roll-Call Accelerators (`components/computer-lab/live-cockpit-bar.tsx`): Jump-to-Roll auto-pan input, Mark All Present, Invert Attendance, and three-tier semantic status badge.
  - Quick Station Popover (`components/computer-lab/station-quick-popover.tsx`): 1-tap floating attendance flip, Tier 2 seat reassign, and direct fault report ticket creation.
  - Official A4 Wall Seating Chart (`app/(dashboard)/print/seating-chart/page.tsx`): Laminated physical room chart grouped by rows A–D with teacher podium.
- **Track 2: Institutional Reporting, Governance & Operational Intelligence**:
  - Canonical Reporting Engine (`app/actions/institutional-reports.ts`): Zero shadow databases. Direct queries for NEB 75% Board Compliance, syllabus quota completion, faculty dual sign-off ledger, lab occupancy index, and workstation MTTR/uptime analytics.
  - Workstation Technical Biography Drawer (`components/analytics/workstation-biography-drawer.tsx`): Complete lifecycle timeline of faults, servicing history, and past student seatings.
  - Triple-Collision Defense Engine (`lib/scheduling/conflict-engine.ts`): Prevents room, faculty, and student cohort double-booking across weekly academic timetable slots.
  - Immutable Audit Ledger (`lib/audit/audit-ledger.ts`): Structured JSONB before/after diff audit trail for roll-call overrides, session seat swaps, and workstation issue lifecycle changes.
  - Official Board Excel Export (`lib/exports/xlsx.ts`): Styled `.xlsx` workbook generation for NEB Practical Attendance & Board Exam Compliance Register with three-tier institutional signatures.
  - Real-Time Derived Reminders Queue (`getInstitutionalReminders`): Live alerts for critical workstation faults, overdue preventive maintenance, and unverified practical sessions.
  - Multi-Year Academic Lifecycle & Cohort Promotion (`app/actions/academic-years.ts`): Single-query aggregations for enrollment counts, atomic cohort promotions with exceptions (repeaters, archived/left), and database status check constraint enforcement.

## 6. Critical User Rules & Terminology Standards

Agents working on this repository **MUST** follow these rules without exception:

### 1. NO Literal `+` in Button Labels
- **RULE**: Never put literal `+` inside button or action text (e.g. `<span>+ Record Service</span>` or `<span>+ Quick Book</span>`).
- **Correct**: `<Plus className="h-4 w-4" /> <span>Record Service</span>`
- **Incorrect**: `<span>+ Record Service</span>`

### 2. Standardized Academic Terminology
- Use **"Attendance"** — **NEVER** "Turnout" or "Turnout Tally".
- Use **"Timetable"** or **"Schedule Grid"** — **NEVER** "Matrix" or "Today's Matrix".
- Use **"Logbook"** — **NEVER** "Ledger" (for maintenance and session logs).
- Use **"Save & Submit Log"** — **NEVER** "Endorse" or "Log Done".
- Use **"Equipment Breakage"** — **NEVER** "Apparatus Breakage".

### 3. Safety Lock: Keep "Precaution Active" Intact
- In the Super Admin console (`/admin`), the safety lock switch that guards sensitive actions (e.g. editing teacher permissions or routines) is called **"Precaution Active"**. Keep this safety toggle and label as-is.

### 4. Zero Pricing/Cost Clutter in Maintenance
- Maintenance plans and service logs are strictly for technical compliance (cleaning, thermal paste, BIOS, updates, hardware checks). Do not re-add financial/budget/pricing fields.

### 5. Zero Department Regressions
- Department strings have been purged from the data model and UI. In user profiles, menus, and lab cards, display **Role Badges** (`super_admin`, `lab_incharge`, `hod`, `teacher`) and **Assigned Lab / Facility Scope**. Never re-add or render `department`.

### 6. Font Loader & CSS Variable Rules
- `Noto_Sans_Devanagari` in Next.js `next/font/google` requires explicit subsets (`subsets: ['devanagari']`) and weights (`weight: ['400', '500', '600', '700']`).
- All 4 font instances must attach their `.variable` classes to `<html className="...">` in `app/layout.tsx`.
- Single Tailwind config: keep `tailwind.config.ts`. Never introduce duplicate `tailwind.config.js` or `.mjs`.

### 7. Performance & Glass Surfaces
- Never apply `backdrop-blur-*` to repeated card grids or list items (causes GPU compositor thrashing on low-end hardware). Use the layered `.glass-card` class instead.
- Reserve backdrop-filter exclusively for single viewport elements like sticky headers (`.glass-header`) or modal dialogs.
- Large KPI metrics must use `font-heading font-extrabold tabular-nums` for executive punch.

### 8. Strict TypeScript Verification
- Always execute `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task to guarantee 0 compile or type errors across all routes and components.

### 9. Semantic Color Palette & Three-Tier Attendance Rules
- **Brand Accent**: Indigo (`--color-accent` / `#6366F1`)
- **Success**: Emerald (`--color-success` / `#10B981`)
- **Warning**: Amber (`--color-warning` / `#F59E0B`) — strictly scoped to items requiring user action (e.g., `Pending Roll-Call`, unlogged past sessions, awaiting review). **NEVER** use amber for nominal attendance.
- **Danger**: Rose (`--color-danger` / `#EF4444`) for critical equipment breakages, major hazards, and critically low attendance.
- **Neutral**: Slate / Zinc scale for all structural text, borders, and nominal states.
- **Attendance Semantic Tiers**:
  - `>= 85%`: Success (Emerald text + emerald badge `Optimal`)
  - `75% - 84%`: Nominal (Neutral slate text + indigo/neutral badge `Normal` — **NO false warning color**)
  - `< 75%`: Danger (Rose text + rose badge `Low Rate`)
  - `0%` / Pending: Neutral dash `—` + neutral badge `Awaiting`

### 10. High-Density Card Pattern: Zero Card-in-Card Nesting
- **No Double-Nesting**: Never wrap individual metric cards inside a parent card container with redundant outer headers or footers.
- **Direct Grid**: Place metric cards directly inside a responsive grid (`grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3 gap-2.5 sm:gap-3`) as standalone top-level `.glass-card` elements.
- **2-Row High-Density Layout (~76px total height)**:
  - Row 1: `h-6 w-6` tinted icon badge + uppercase title (left) | status pill (right).
  - Row 2: Bold punchy metric (`text-xl sm:text-[22px] font-extrabold font-heading`) on left | micro-context / progress bar on right.
  - Padding must remain compact: `p-2.5 sm:p-3`.

### 11. Dashboard Layout Symmetry & Height Alignment
- In the 2-column continuous command center (`lg:grid-cols-12`):
  - Left Column (`lg:col-span-8`): Holds Practical Operations KPI cards, Live Session Cockpit, and Segmented Session Feed.
  - Right Column (`lg:col-span-4`): Holds Quick Operations, Facility Rooms Telemetry, and Incident Registry.
  - Top-Fold Alignment: The left column's 3 KPI cards (~76px) and the right column's `QuickOperationsCard` (~76px) must maintain matching heights.
  - Queue Capping: Default queue lists capped at 4 items (`MAX_UPCOMING_DEFAULT = 4`) with an expandable toggle.

### 12. Universal "Equipment" Standard (Zero "Apparatus")
- The term "Apparatus" is strictly forbidden. Always use **"Equipment"** across all schemas, UI components, modals, filters, and exports.

### 13. Next.js `'use server'` RPC Export Rules
- Files marked with `'use server'` (`app/actions/*`) MUST ONLY export `async function`s.
- Domain constants, types, and synchronous validators belong in pure TypeScript modules in `lib/` (e.g. `lib/lab-status.ts`).

### 14. Lab Facility Status Lifecycle & Server-Side Enforcement
- Allowed Statuses: `'Operational' | 'Under Maintenance' | 'Inactive'` (validated by database constraint `labs_status_check`).
- Derived Active Lifecycle: `is_active = (status === 'Operational')`.
- Server Guard Requirement: Server actions (`createSchedule`, `createPracticalLog`) MUST query PostgreSQL directly and reject attempts to book or log practicals for non-operational labs.

### 15. Incident Category Referential Integrity
- Categories referenced by past incidents must be soft-archived (`is_active = false`) rather than hard-deleted.

### 16. Zero Shadow Databases
- All institutional analytics and reporting MUST query live PostgreSQL tables (`practical_logs`, `schedules`, `workstation_issues`, `student_enrollments`, `students`). Never introduce redundant reporting datastores or caching replicas that drift from operational state.

### 17. Triple-Collision Defense Invariant
- Every timetable slot and ad-hoc live session booking MUST be validated by `detectScheduleCollisions` in `lib/scheduling/conflict-engine.ts` across three independent dimensions:
  1. Room Collision (same lab, overlapping time slot, same day)
  2. Faculty Collision (same teacher, overlapping time slot, same day)
  3. Cohort Collision (same class/grade cohort, overlapping time slot, same day)

### 18. Student Enrollment Status Check Constraints
- In `public.student_enrollments`, the `status` column has a strict check constraint:
  `CHECK (status IN ('active', 'transferred', 'graduated', 'archived', 'completed'))`.
  Never use unapproved statuses (e.g. `'retained'`, `'promoted'`). Use `'active'` for new/repeating enrollments, `'archived'` for completed prior years, and `'transferred'` for departing students.

### 19. Workstation Status Derivation
- `public.workstations` does NOT have a `status` column. Workstation operational state is dynamically derived by inspecting `public.workstation_issues`:
  - `status = 'in_progress'` &rarr; `under_repair`
  - `status = 'open'` &rarr; `flagged`
  - No active issues &rarr; `operational`

### 20. Node.js Test Execution Protocol
- Test suites in `tests/*.test.mjs` must load `.env.local` into `process.env` at initialization so `resolveDatabaseUrl()` connects with SSL enabled.
- Run tests using:
  `node --experimental-strip-types --import ./tests/register-hooks.mjs --test <test_path>`

### 21. Future UI Redesign Initiative (Stitch.google.com)
- When prompted by the user to redesign the UI or modernize components with Stitch (`stitch.google.com`), refer to [doc/plans/REMINDER_UI_REDESIGN_WITH_STITCH_GOOGLE.md](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/doc/plans/REMINDER_UI_REDESIGN_WITH_STITCH_GOOGLE.md) for the target screens, design system tokens, and reapplication workflow.

### 22. Sequential Task Documentation & Pre-flight Review
- **Authoritative Register**: After completing any major feature or architectural task, agents MUST create a sequentially numbered task log in `doc/tasks/` (e.g. `doc/tasks/2026-10-11-task-XX-<title>.md`) and update the master index in [doc/tasks/README.md](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/doc/tasks/README.md).
- **Mandatory Pre-flight Review**: Before starting any new task, agents MUST review [doc/tasks/README.md](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/doc/tasks/README.md) and read relevant task files to preserve established invariants and avoid regressions.

### 23. Institutional Holiday & Weekly Recess Invariant
- **Authoritative Policy Engine**: Laboratory practical operations and attendance tallies are automatically suspended on institutional holidays (e.g., Bada Dashain, Tihar, Constitution Day) as well as statutory Saturday weekends and when the Sunday Week Off Policy is active.
- **Single Source of Truth**: All client views and server actions must validate dates against [lib/calendar-policy.ts](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/lib/calendar-policy.ts) (`evaluateDateSuspension` and `checkServerDateSuspension`).
- **Live Cockpit Invariant**: On suspended dates, `/computer-lab` MUST NOT auto-select routine slots, MUST NOT display roll-call glowing rings or "Save & Submit Practical Log" actions, and MUST display the official **Institutional Recess / Holiday Suspension Card**.
- **Server Guard Requirement**: Both `submitLiveSession` and `createPracticalLog` MUST reject any attempts to submit practical logs on suspended dates.

# you asked

message time: 2026-10-16 13:03:54

### Domain 1: Database & Backend Data Layer
1. **Database Indexing:** Are frequently queried, filtered (`WHERE`), sorted (`ORDER BY`), and joined foreign keys explicitly indexed? Flag missing composite indexes.
​2. **N+1 Query Detection:** Are ORM calls (Prisma, TypeORM, Hibernate, ActiveRecord, etc.) executing separate sub-queries inside loops instead of using eager joins, batch fetching, or dataloaders?
3. **Expensive Query & Computation Caching:** Are resource-heavy aggregations or repetitive queries cached (e.g., via Redis, Memcached, or materialized views) with appropriate TTLs?
4. **Database Connection Pooling:** Is there an active pool configuration (e.g., PgBouncer, HikariCP, Prisma connection limits) to prevent connection starvation under concurrent spikes?
5. **Pagination of Large Datasets:** Are all multi-record endpoints strictly paginated (cursor-based or limit/offset)? Flag unbounded `.findAll()` or `SELECT *` without limits.

### Domain 2: Network, Edge & Infrastructure
6. **API Response Caching:** Are read-heavy HTTP endpoints returning appropriate cache directives (`Cache-Control`, `ETag`, `stale-while-revalidate`) or edge/reverse-proxy cache policies?
7. **API Payload Compression:** Is compression middleware (`Brotli` / `Gzip`) active on the web/API gateway for JSON payloads and static responses?
8. **CDN Distribution:** Are static assets (JS, CSS, images, media) served via a globally distributed CDN with aggressive caching headers?
9. **Load Balancing & Horizontal Scaling:** Is traffic routed through a load balancer (ALB, Nginx, Cloudflare) with clear health check configurations and session persistence strategy?
10. **Server-Side Application Caching:** Is in-memory or distributed caching utilized for rendered HTML fragments, token lookups, or user session state?

### Domain 3: Frontend Runtime & Interaction
11. **Unnecessary Component Re-renders:** Are UI components re-rendering unnecessarily due to unstable object references, missing memoization (`useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo`), or bloated context state?
12. **Input Debouncing & Throttling:** Are search inputs, window resize handlers, scroll events, and autosave calls debounced or throttled to prevent event-loop congestion?
13. **Loading Skeletons & Layout Stability:** Are perceived loading states handled with structural skeleton loaders rather than blocking spinners or content shifts that harm CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)?

### Domain 4: Asset Delivery, Bundling & Core Web Vitals
14. **Asset Lazy Loading:** Are below-the-fold images, offscreen iframes, and hidden heavy components lazy-loaded via native `loading="lazy"` or dynamic imports?
15. **Image Optimization & Compression:** Are modern formats (`WebP`, `AVIF`) enforced, images responsive (`srcset`), and raw uploads auto-compressed before delivery?
16. **Code Splitting & Dynamic Chunks:** Is code split at the route level and heavy modal/subsystem level (e.g., `React.lazy`, dynamic `import()`) to keep the initial bundle small?
17. **JS/CSS Minification:** Is the production build pipeline configured to aggressively strip dead code, minify, and mangle bundle outputs?
18. **Non-Critical Script Deferral:** Are third-party scripts (analytics, trackers, widgets) loaded asynchronously or deferred (`async`, `defer`, or dedicated script loaders)?
19. **Unused Dependencies & Tree-Shaking:** Are there bloated imports (e.g., importing entire `lodash` instead of `lodash-es` or specific utils) and packages that can be pruned?
20. **Lighthouse & Core Web Vitals Readiness:** Are there immediate blockers for LCP (<2.5s), INP (<200ms), and CLS (<0.1)?

### Audit Output Format
Present your analysis as:
- **Executive Summary:** Overall performance grade (A-F) and top 3 critical bottlenecks.
- **Detailed Audit Table:** Checkpoint | Status (Pass / Fail / Warn) | High-Level Finding.
- **Remediation Plan:** Prioritized step-by-step code and config patches starting with Highest Impact / Lowest Effort.

# gemini response

## Executive Summary

**Overall Performance Grade: C+**

The **LabSync LIMS** architecture demonstrates strong foundational engineering in several areas: it implements a singleton `pg.Pool` routed through Supabase’s transaction-mode connection pooler (port `6543`), utilizes `next/dynamic` to split heavy administrative subsystems out of the initial bundle, and provides custom route-level `loading.tsx` skeletons. 

However, production scalability and runtime responsiveness are bottlenecked by **three critical issues**:
1. **Unpooled `pg.Client` Instantiation & Sequential N+1 Loops in Server Actions:** Authentication (`app/actions/auth.ts`) and OTP (`app/actions/otp.ts`) actions bypass the shared `getPgPool()` singleton and spin up raw `new pg.Client()` TCP/SSL handshakes on every call. Furthermore, log creation (`app/actions/logs.ts`), floor element updates (`app/actions/floor-elements.ts`), and cohort promotions (`app/actions/academic-years.ts`) execute sequential `await` queries inside `for...of` loops.
2. **1Hz Global Re-render Cascade (`useLiveSchedule`):** `hooks/use-live-schedule.ts` runs a `1000ms` `setInterval` that updates `now` state every second, triggering full-tree re-renders and recalculating Bikram Sambat calendar conversions, period ranges, and array sorting on every tick.
3. **Un-debounced Server Action Filter Queries:** Search inputs in `app/(dashboard)/records/incidents/page.tsx` and `app/(dashboard)/records/page.tsx` bind directly to `filters.search`, which sits in a `useEffect` dependency array that invokes database-backed Server Actions (`getIncidentRecords`, `getPracticalRecords`) and `window.history.replaceState` on every keystroke.

## Remediation Plan

### Priority 1: Highest Impact / Lowest Effort (Immediate Quick Wins)

#### 1. Replace Raw `pg.Client` with Shared `getPgPool()` in Auth & OTP Actions (Domain 1.4)
**Bottleneck:** `app/actions/auth.ts` and `app/actions/otp.ts` call `getPgClient()`, which creates a brand-new `new pg.Client()` TCP + SSL connection on every invocation. Under concurrent login or registration spikes, this exhausts PostgreSQL connections and adds 150–300ms of SSL handshake latency per request.
**Patch (`app/actions/auth.ts` & `app/actions/otp.ts`):**
```typescript
// REMOVE getPgClient() from app/actions/auth.ts and app/actions/otp.ts:
// function getPgClient() { return new pg.Client(...) }

// REPLACE single queries with getPgPool().query():
import { getPgPool } from '@/lib/db'

export async function toggleUserActiveStatus(userId: string, is_active: boolean) {
  const scope = await getServerUserScope()
  if (scope.role !== 'super_admin') {
    return { success: false, error: 'Access Denied' }
  }

  const pool = getPgPool()
  const prevRes = await pool.query(
    `SELECT id, full_name, role, is_active FROM public.profiles WHERE id = $1::uuid`,
    [userId]
  )
  const beforeProfile = prevRes.rows[0] || null

  await pool.query(
    `UPDATE public.profiles SET is_active = $1 WHERE id = $2::uuid`,
    [is_active, userId]
  )
  // ... audit & revalidate
}

// For multi-statement transactions (e.g., deleteUserAccount, verifySignupAndCreateAccount),
// checkout a pooled client and release it in `finally`:
const pool = getPgPool()
const client = await pool.connect()
try {
  await client.query('BEGIN')
  // ... transactional queries ...
  await client.query('COMMIT')
} catch (e) {
  await client.query('ROLLBACK')
  throw e
} finally {
  client.release() // Returns connection to pool instead of closing TCP socket
}
```

#### 2. Parallelize Sequential Server Queries in `ComputerLabPage` (Domain 4.20 - LCP)
**Bottleneck:** `app/(dashboard)/computer-lab/page.tsx` runs 4 independent queries (`getWorkstationBoardData`, `labs`, `schedules`, `classes`, `class_subjects`) sequentially, delaying Time to First Byte (TTFB) and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP).
**Patch (`app/(dashboard)/computer-lab/page.tsx`):**
```typescript
export default async function ComputerLabPage() {
  const supabase = await createClient()
  const scope = await getServerUserScope()
  const pool = getPgPool()

  // Execute all 5 independent data fetches concurrently
  const [
    initialBoardData,
    labRes,
    { data: schedRows },
    { data: classesData },
    { data: csRows },
  ] = await Promise.all([
    getWorkstationBoardData('comp'),
    pool
      .query('SELECT id, name, code, capacity, type, status, is_active FROM public.labs WHERE id = $1 LIMIT 1', ['comp'])
      .catch(() => ({ rows: [] })),
    (supabase.from('schedules') as any)
      .select(`
        id, lab_id, teacher_id, start_time, end_time, day_key, class_subject_id,
        class_subjects:class_subject_id (
          id, class_id, subject_id, teacher_id,
          classes:class_id ( id, name, grade, section ),
          subjects:subject_id ( id, code, name ),
          profiles:teacher_id ( id, full_name )
        )
      `)
      .eq('lab_id', 'comp')
      .order('start_time', { ascending: true }),
    (supabase.from('classes') as any)
      .select('id, name, grade, section')
      .order('grade', { ascending: true }),
    (supabase.from('class_subjects') as any)
      .select(`
        id, class_id, subject_id, teacher_id,
        classes:class_id ( id, name ),
        subjects:subject_id ( id, code, name )
      `),
  ])
  // ... transform and render
}
```

  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    setDebouncedFilters(filters)

}, [filters])

  fetchIncidents(true)

const pool = getPgPool()
await pool.query(
  `UPDATE public.log_attendance la
   SET enrollment_id = se.id,
       student_id = se.student_id
   FROM public.student_enrollments se
   WHERE la.log_id = $1
     AND la.enrollment_id IS NULL
     AND se.academic_year_id = $2
     AND se.class_id = $3
     AND se.status = 'active'
     AND la.roll_number = se.roll_number;`,
  [recordId, effectiveYearId, targetClassId]

**Patch (`app/actions/floor-elements.ts`):**

// Batch upsert all floor landmarks in a single query:
const toUpsert = elements.map((el) => {

#### 6. Add Missing Composite & Trigram Indexes to PostgreSQL (Domain 1.1)
**Bottleneck:** Frequent multi-column filters (`student_enrollments`, `practical_logs`, `workstation_seat_plans`) and `ILIKE '%search%'` queries lack composite and GIN trigram indexes.
**Migration SQL Patch:**
```sql
-- Enable pg_trgm for fast ILIKE '%...%' searches
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

-- 1. Composite indexes for hot foreign-key + filter lookups
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_student_enrollments_year_class_status
  ON public.student_enrollments (academic_year_id, class_id, status, roll_number);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_practical_logs_year_lab_date
  ON public.practical_logs (academic_year_id, lab_id, date DESC, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_practical_logs_schedule_date
  ON public.practical_logs (schedule_id, date);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_lab_incidents_lab_status_date
  ON public.lab_incidents (lab_id, status, severity, date DESC);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_workstation_issues_ws_status
  ON public.workstation_issues (workstation_id, status, severity);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_logs_entity_action_created
  ON public.audit_logs (entity_type, action, created_at DESC);

-- 2. GIN Trigram indexes for ILIKE '%search%' filters
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_practical_logs_search_trgm
  ON public.practical_logs USING gin (practical_title gin_trgm_ops, subject_name gin_trgm_ops, batch_group gin_trgm_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_students_name_trgm
  ON public.students USING gin (full_name gin_trgm_ops, admission_no gin_trgm_ops);
```

# LabSync LIMS — Master Implementation Plan: Production Hardening & Performance Optimization

> **Status**: Ready for Verification & Approval  
> **Target System**: LabSync LIMS (`d:\Projects\LMR`)  
> **Audience**: Project Owner / Lab In-Charge & Lead Systems Architect  
> **Frameworks**: Next.js 16.3.3 App Router, React 19, Supabase PostgreSQL, Tailwind CSS v4  
> **Guiding Principle**: Zero data loss, zero disruptions to active academic timetables, and strict adherence to institutional standards (`AGENTS.md`).

---

## Executive Overview

This master implementation plan synthesizes the findings of two comprehensive investigations:
1. **The Phase 0 Audit**: Addressed institutional security, authentication vulnerabilities, wide-open database tables, and access control.
2. **The Gemini Performance & Scale Audit (Domains 1–4)**: Addressed database indexing, N+1 query loops, connection pool leakage, 1-second re-render cascades, and un-debounced search queries.

The plan is divided into **6 surgical, sequential phases**. Each phase is self-contained, testable, and designed so that no change breaks existing school operations.

```mermaid
graph LR
    P1["Phase 1: Critical Security Hotfixes"] --> P2["Phase 2: Database & Query Performance"]
    P2 --> P3["Phase 3: Frontend Runtime & Web Vitals"]
    P3 --> P4["Phase 4: Architecture & Mock Purge"]
    P4 --> P5["Phase 5: Media & Storage Migration"]
    P5 --> P6["Phase 6: Comprehensive Verification"]
```

---

## Phase 1: Zero-Risk Urgent Security Hotfixes

> **Objective**: Eliminate immediate security exploits that allow unauthorized access or timetable alteration. All items in this phase have **low regression risk** because they align database policies with intended institutional permissions.

---

### Task 1.1: Restrict Self-Role Escalation on `public.profiles` (FIND-SEC-01)
* **Files**: `schema.sql`, PostgreSQL migration
* **Plain Language Explanation**:
  Currently, any logged-in teacher can send an update request to change their own role to `super_admin` because the database rule checks *who* you are, but doesn't check *what* columns you are allowed to change.
* **Technical Remediation**:
  1. Revoke column-level update privileges for `role`, `approval_status`, `permissions`, and `is_active` from the `authenticated` role on `public.profiles`.
  2. Implement a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger function on `public.profiles` (`protect_profile_escalation`) ensuring only active Super Admins can alter role or approval status.
* **Verification**:
  Execute a test `PATCH` to `/rest/v1/profiles` using a teacher token attempting to set `{"role": "super_admin"}` — must return `403 Forbidden` / error.

---

### Task 1.2: Remove `internalBypassScopeCheck` from Public Server Actions (FIND-SEC-02)
* **Files**:
  * [`app/actions/academic-years.ts`](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/app/actions/academic-years.ts#L225)
  * [`app/actions/archive-hub.ts`](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/app/actions/archive-hub.ts#L29)
  * [`app/actions/seat-plans.ts`](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/app/actions/seat-plans.ts#L66)
* **Plain Language Explanation**:
  Server Actions in Next.js are publicly callable API endpoints. Several actions had an optional parameter called `internalBypassScopeCheck`. Anyone sending `{ "internalBypassScopeCheck": true }` from their browser console could bypass administrator authorization checks.
* **Technical Remediation**:
  1. Strip `internalBypassScopeCheck` from all exported Server Action parameter types and inputs.
  2. Split internal workflows (e.g. background maintenance or system seeding) into unexported internal helper functions (e.g., `_internalPromoteCohort`) that are not callable from the browser.
* **Verification**:
  Attempt calling `archiveStudentAction` with `{ internalBypassScopeCheck: true }` under a teacher role — must be strictly rejected with `Access Denied`.

---

### Task 1.3: Generate and Enforce Cryptographic `TERMINAL_SIGNING_SECRET` (FIND-SEC-03)
* **Files**:
  * `.env.local`
  * [`lib/security/terminal-token.ts`](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/lib/security/terminal-token.ts#L9-L13)
* **Plain Language Explanation**:
  The security key used to sign student workstation login cookies and terminal handshakes was falling back to a hardcoded string visible in the code (`labsync-lims-default-terminal-signing-salt-2083`). A clever student on campus could use this to forge attendance for any desk in the Computer Lab.
* **Technical Remediation**:
  1. Generate a high-entropy 256-bit random secret (`openssl rand -hex 32`).
  2. Add `TERMINAL_SIGNING_SECRET=<secret>` to `.env.local`.
  3. Update `lib/security/terminal-token.ts` to require `process.env.TERMINAL_SIGNING_SECRET` and throw a descriptive startup error if missing, rather than silently using a hardcoded string.
* **Verification**:
  Verify existing terminal handshake tests pass with the real environment secret loaded.

### Task 1.5: Lock Down Open Database Tables in PostgreSQL RLS (FIND-SEC-05, 06, 07, 08, 11)
* **Files**: `schema.sql`, PostgreSQL migration
* **Plain Language Explanation**:
  Several tables (`labs`, `schedules`, `calendar_settings`, `audit_logs`, `log_attendance`, and `teacher_substitutions`) had permissive rules allowing any anonymous visitor to write or delete records without logging in.
* **Technical Remediation**:
  1. `public.labs`: Drop `"Allow insert/update labs"`. Require `is_privileged()` for `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE`. Allow public `SELECT` for active labs.
  2. `public.schedules`: Drop `"Allow manage schedules"`. Restrict writes to `is_privileged()` administrators.
  3. `public.calendar_settings`: Restrict writes to `is_privileged()`.
  4. `public.audit_logs`: Revoke direct `INSERT` from `anon` and `authenticated`; insert only via server-side connection pool.
  5. `public.teacher_substitutions`: Allow teachers to manage only their own substitutions; administrators can manage all.
* **Verification**:
  Run Supabase RLS test scripts verifying that unauthenticated curl requests cannot modify or delete schedules or calendar settings.

## Phase 2: Database & Query Performance (Domain 1)

> **Objective**: Eliminate database connection socket leaks, add high-speed database indexes, remove 40-step sequential N+1 loops, and prevent unbounded memory queries.

---

### Task 2.1: Unify Database Connection Pooling (FIND-REL-01 / Domain 1.4)
* **Files**:
  * [`app/actions/auth.ts`](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/app/actions/auth.ts#L20-L29)
  * [`app/actions/otp.ts`](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/app/actions/otp.ts#L26)
* **Plain Language Explanation**:
  Most of the application uses a shared "connection pool" (like a shared fleet of vehicles). But user signups and profile actions were spinning up a brand new, unmanaged connection every time. When an error occurred, the connection was never closed, eventually consuming all available database slots.
* **Technical Remediation**:
  1. Remove `getPgClient()` from `auth.ts` and `otp.ts`.
  2. Import and use `getPgPool()` from `lib/db.ts` across all 12 query locations.
  3. For multi-statement transactions (e.g. signup flow), acquire a pooled client using `const client = await pool.connect()` and guarantee its release in a `finally` block:
     ```typescript
     const pool = getPgPool()
     const client = await pool.connect()
     try {
       await client.query('BEGIN')
       // ... transactional queries ...
       await client.query('COMMIT')
     } catch (err) {
       await client.query('ROLLBACK')
       throw err
     } finally {
       client.release() // Returns connection to the pool
     }
     ```
* **Verification**:
  Simulate 15 concurrent invalid registration requests — verify zero open connection leaks in PostgreSQL `pg_stat_activity`.

---

### Task 2.2: Add Missing Composite & B-Tree Indexes to PostgreSQL (Domain 1.1)
* **Files**: `schema.sql`, PostgreSQL migration
* **Plain Language Explanation**:
  The system's most heavily used tables (`practical_logs`, `lab_incidents`, `maintenance_logs`) currently have zero custom indexes. The database has to scan every single historical row every time someone views a record.
* **Technical Remediation**:
  Deploy the following index migrations:
  ```sql
  -- 1. Practical Logs (Hot analytical and history lookups)
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_practical_logs_lookup 
    ON public.practical_logs (lab_id, academic_year_id, date DESC);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_practical_logs_schedule_date 
    ON public.practical_logs (schedule_id, date);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_practical_logs_teacher 
    ON public.practical_logs (teacher_id, date DESC);

  -- 2. Log Attendance (Relational bridge and roll lookup)
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_log_attendance_log_roll 
    ON public.log_attendance (log_id, roll_number);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_log_attendance_enrollment 
    ON public.log_attendance (enrollment_id);

  -- 3. Incident Registry (Status triage & date filtering)
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_lab_incidents_lookup 
    ON public.lab_incidents (lab_id, status, date DESC);

  -- 4. Timetable & Maintenance
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_schedules_lab_day 
    ON public.schedules (lab_id, day_of_week);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_maintenance_logs_lab 
    ON public.maintenance_logs (lab_id, performed_at DESC);
  ```
* **Verification**:
  Run `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on practical log queries — verify sequential scans convert to Index Scans with execution time dropping from ~45ms to <2ms.

### Task 2.3: Eliminate 40-Step N+1 Attendance Bridging Loop in `logs.ts` (Domain 1.2)
* **Files**:
  * [`app/actions/logs.ts`](file:///d:/Projects/LMR/app/actions/logs.ts#L734-L744)
* **Plain Language Explanation**:
  When a teacher saves attendance for a class of 40 students, the server currently sends 40 individual database requests one after another. This makes saving practical logs sluggish and prone to network hiccups.
* **Technical Remediation**:
  Replace the JavaScript `for (const enr of enrollments)` loop with a single atomic SQL join update:
  ```typescript
  const pool = getPgPool()
  await pool.query(
    `UPDATE public.log_attendance la
     SET enrollment_id = se.id,
         student_id = se.student_id
     FROM public.student_enrollments se
     WHERE la.log_id = $1
       AND la.enrollment_id IS NULL
       AND se.academic_year_id = $2
       AND se.class_id = $3
       AND se.status = 'active'
       AND la.roll_number = se.roll_number;`,
    [recordId, effectiveYearId, targetClassId]
  )
  ```
* **Verification**:
  Submit a practical log for Class 11 Science (35+ students) — confirm the attendance bridge executes in a single database round-trip in <50ms.

import { createServerClient, type CookieOptions } from '@supabase/ssr'
import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from 'next/server'

export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const { pathname } = request.nextUrl

  let response = NextResponse.next({
    request: {
      headers: request.headers,
    },
  })

  const supabaseUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
  const supabaseAnonKey =
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY ||
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY

  // If Supabase is not configured, allow pass-through for development
  if (!supabaseUrl || !supabaseAnonKey || supabaseUrl.includes('dummy-project')) {
    return response
  }

  try {
    const supabase = createServerClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey, {
      cookies: {
        getAll() {
          return request.cookies.getAll()
        },
        setAll(cookiesToSet) {
          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) => request.cookies.set(name, value))
          response = NextResponse.next({
            request: {
              headers: request.headers,
            },
          })
          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>
            response.cookies.set({
              name,
              value,
              ...options,
            })
          )
        },
      },
    })

    const {
      data: { user },
    } = await supabase.auth.getUser()

    // 1. If user is authenticated:
    if (user) {
      // Fast path for Server Action RPCs: authenticated actions handle their own granular RBAC server-side
      if (request.headers.has('next-action')) {
        return response
      }

      // Query user profile to verify active status and role on page navigations
      const { data: profile } = await supabase
        .from('profiles')
        .select('role, is_active, approval_status')
        .eq('id', user.id)
        .single()

      const isActive = (profile as any)?.is_active ?? true
      const role = (profile as any)?.role || 'teacher'
      const approvalStatus = (profile as any)?.approval_status

      // 1. Check if user is deactivated
      if (!isActive) {
        if (request.headers.has('next-action')) {
          return new NextResponse(
            JSON.stringify({ error: 'Account deactivated' }),
            { status: 403, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }
          )
        }
        const redirectUrl = new URL('/login?error=account_deactivated', request.url)
        return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl)
      }

      // 2. Check if user is rejected
      if (approvalStatus === 'rejected') {
        if (request.headers.has('next-action')) {
          return new NextResponse(
            JSON.stringify({ error: 'Account registration rejected' }),
            { status: 403, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }
          )
        }
        const redirectUrl = new URL('/login?error=account_rejected', request.url)
        return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl)
      }

      // 3. Strict Profile Lockdown for Non-Approved Accounts (pending or awaiting review):
      // Users without verified administrator approval are confined strictly to /profile
      if (approvalStatus !== 'approved') {
        if (pathname !== '/profile') {
          const redirectUrl = new URL('/profile?notice=pending_verification', request.url)
          return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl)
        }
      }

      // Check Super Admin route protection
      if (pathname.startsWith('/admin')) {
        if (role !== 'super_admin' || approvalStatus !== 'approved' || !isActive) {
          // Unauthorized: redirect to dashboard root
          if (request.headers.has('next-action')) {
            return new NextResponse(
              JSON.stringify({ error: 'Unauthorized admin access' }),
              { status: 403, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }
            )
          }
          const redirectUrl = new URL('/?error=unauthorized_admin_access', request.url)
          return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl)
        }
      }

      // Check Maintenance route protection
      if (pathname.startsWith('/maintenance')) {
        const canAccessMaintenance =
          role === 'super_admin' ||
          role === 'lab_incharge' ||
          role === 'hod' ||
          (role as string) === 'coordinator' ||
          (profile as any)?.permissions?.can_manage_maintenance === true

        if (!canAccessMaintenance || approvalStatus !== 'approved' || !isActive) {
          if (request.headers.has('next-action')) {
            return new NextResponse(
              JSON.stringify({ error: 'Unauthorized maintenance access' }),
              { status: 403, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }
            )
          }
          const redirectUrl = new URL('/?error=unauthorized_maintenance_access', request.url)
          return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl)
        }
      }

      // If user is already authenticated and visits /login, redirect
      if (pathname === '/login') {
        const dest = approvalStatus !== 'approved' ? '/profile' : '/'
        const redirectUrl = new URL(dest, request.url)
        return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl)
      }
    } else {
      // 2. If user is unauthenticated:
      // Protect internal pages
      const isProtected =
        pathname === '/' ||
        pathname.startsWith('/admin') ||
        pathname.startsWith('/incidents') ||
        pathname.startsWith('/records') ||
        pathname.startsWith('/schedules') ||
        pathname.startsWith('/logs') ||
        pathname.startsWith('/maintenance') ||
        pathname.startsWith('/computer-lab') ||
        pathname.startsWith('/print')

      if (isProtected) {
        // Do not redirect Server Action RPC requests to HTML login page (avoids Flight parsing errors)
        if (request.headers.has('next-action')) {
          return new NextResponse(
            JSON.stringify({ error: 'Unauthorized. Please sign in.' }),
            { status: 401, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }
          )
        }

        const redirectUrl = new URL(
          `/login?redirect=${encodeURIComponent(pathname)}`,
          request.url
        )
        return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl)
      }
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn('Middleware auth verification error:', error)

    const isProtected =
      pathname === '/' ||
      pathname.startsWith('/admin') ||
      pathname.startsWith('/incidents') ||
      pathname.startsWith('/records') ||
      pathname.startsWith('/schedules') ||
      pathname.startsWith('/logs') ||
      pathname.startsWith('/maintenance') ||
      pathname.startsWith('/computer-lab') ||
      pathname.startsWith('/print')

    if (isProtected) {
      if (request.headers.has('next-action')) {
        return new NextResponse(
          JSON.stringify({ error: 'Session expired or authentication failed. Please sign in.' }),
          { status: 401, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }
        )
      }
      const redirectUrl = new URL(
        `/login?error=session_expired&redirect=${encodeURIComponent(pathname)}`,
        request.url
      )
      return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl)
    }
  }

  return response
}

export const config = {
  matcher: [
    /*
     * Match all request paths except for:
     * - _next/static (static files)
     * - _next/image (image optimization files)
     * - favicon.ico (favicon file)
     * - images / icons
     */
    '/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp)$).*)',
  ],
}

FILE: PRD.md

# Product Requirements Document (PRD)
## Project Name: LabSync — Institutional Laboratory Management System (LIMS / LMR)

- **Target Persona**: Lab In-Charge, Department Heads (HOD), Subject Instructors, and Institutional Super Admins at academic colleges and higher secondary institutions (Classes 11 & 12, undergraduate science & engineering laboratories in Nepal).
- **Primary Tech Stack**: Next.js 16+ (App Router, React 19, Server Components & Server Actions), TypeScript (Strict Mode), Tailwind CSS, Radix UI Primitives, Supabase PostgreSQL, ExcelJS.
- **Calendar Support**: Dual Gregorian (AD) and Bikram Sambat (BS) Nepali Calendar Engine (`nepali-date-converter`, `lib/nepali-calendar.ts`).
- **Design Theme**: Deep Obsidian & Midnight Slate (Dark: Canvas `#0B0F19`, Surface `#101726`) / Pearl Slate (Light: `#F8FAFC`) with specular milled chamfer highlights, layered `.glass-card` surfaces, and tactile micro-physics.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Academic science and technology laboratories (Computer, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Electronics) frequently struggle with manual paper logbooks, session slot collisions, untracked equipment damage, ad-hoc maintenance neglect, and cumbersome attendance tallying during institutional handovers.

**LabSync LIMS** digitizes and modernizes laboratory operations through a single, cohesive institutional platform:
1. **Academic Practical Operations**: Real-time Sunday–Friday timetable routines, Class 11/12 batch attendance tallying, syllabus progress tracking, and dual sign-off (Subject Teacher + Lab In-Charge audit verification).
2. **Interactive CAD Floor Plan & Workstation Cockpit**: Clamped pan/zoom CAD floor viewport, 34-node minimap radar, chamfered living LCD nodes with status LEDs, high-speed roll-call accelerators (`Jump-to-Roll`, `Mark All Present`, `Invert`), and quick station popovers.
3. **Laboratory Infrastructure & Maintenance**: Interactive visual matrix inspections, recurring maintenance SOP routines (thermal paste, deep PC cleaning, BIOS updates, glassware checks), automated due-date reminders, and digital service certification.
4. **Institutional Reporting & Board Exam Intelligence**: Canonical PostgreSQL queries (zero shadow databases) computing NEB 75% practical attendance compliance, syllabus completion quotas, faculty dual sign-off rate, 36 hr/wk lab room occupancy, and workstation MTTR/uptime hotspots.
5. **Triple-Collision Defense & Audit Ledger**: Pre-flight collision engine preventing Room, Faculty, and Student Cohort double-booking across weekly timetable and ad-hoc practical slots, coupled with an immutable structured JSONB diff audit ledger.
6. **Multi-Year Academic Lifecycle & Cohort Promotion**: Multi-year student roll management, atomic cohort promotion from Grade 11 to Grade 12 with repeater and transfer exceptions, and database status check constraint enforcement.
7. **Institutional Handover & Multi-Format Exports**: Official NEB Board Exam styled `.xlsx` workbooks with three-tier signature blocks, raw CSV exports, and high-fidelity A4 landscape print sheets (`@media print` protected).

---

## 2. User Roles & Permissions (RBAC)

Role-based access control is strictly enforced at the server action and UI component layers (`lib/permissions.ts`, `hooks/use-user-scope.ts`):

| Role | Access Level | Primary Focus & Permissions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Super Admin** (`super_admin`) | Full Root Access | User approvals & credential management, role assignments, system reset, timetable configuration, maintenance routine presets, academic year lifecycle & cohort promotions, institution settings, guarded by the **Precaution Active** safety lock. |
| **Lab In-Charge** (`lab_incharge`) | Laboratory Operations | Full Maintenance Workbench (`/maintenance`), CAD floor plan, workstation matrix inspections, incident triage & repair settlements, attendance verification, routine execution, and daily print sheets. |
| **Head of Dept** (`hod`) | Department Oversight | Department-wide practical audits, incident escalations, syllabus quota/pace review, board exam compliance analytics, and certified academic reports. |
| **Teacher / Faculty** (`teacher`) | Instructor Access | 1-click practical logging (`/logs/new`), Live Lab Cockpit roll-call, viewing assigned timetable slots, student attendance roll-call, and reporting equipment breakages. |

> **Note on Data Model Integrity**: Legacy "department" strings have been completely purged from the user model. Faculty and administrators are scoped exclusively via **Role Badges** and **Assigned Laboratory / Facility Scope**.

---

## 3. Database Schema Specification (Supabase PostgreSQL)

```sql
-- ENUMS
create type user_role as enum ('super_admin', 'lab_incharge', 'hod', 'teacher');
create type approval_status as enum ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected');
create type lab_type as enum ('computer_lab', 'physics_lab', 'chemistry_lab', 'biology_lab', 'electronics_lab');
create type session_status as enum ('scheduled', 'in_progress', 'completed', 'cancelled', 'skipped');
create type incident_severity as enum ('minor', 'moderate', 'major_critical');
create type incident_status as enum ('reported', 'investigating', 'resolved', 'escalated_to_hod');
create type maintenance_cadence as enum ('daily', 'weekly', 'biweekly', 'monthly', 'quarterly', 'semester', 'yearly');
create type maintenance_status as enum ('pending', 'overdue', 'completed', 'snoozed');

-- 1. PROFILES TABLE (Zero department clutter; Scoped RBAC)
create table profiles (
  id uuid references auth.users on delete cascade primary key,
  full_name text not null,
  email text not null unique,
  role user_role default 'teacher',
  approval_status approval_status default 'pending',
  permissions jsonb default '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 2. LAB ROOMS & FACILITIES (Status Lifecycle)
create table labs (
  id text primary key,
  name text not null,
  type lab_type not null,
  capacity int not null default 36,
  status text not null default 'Operational' check (status in ('Operational', 'Under Maintenance', 'Inactive')),
  is_active boolean default true,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 3. ACADEMIC YEARS
create table academic_years (
  id text primary key, -- e.g. '2083'
  name text not null, -- e.g. '2083/84'
  start_date text not null,
  end_date text not null,
  is_current boolean default false,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 4. CLASSES & CURRICULAR MAPPING
create table classes (
  id text primary key, -- e.g. '11sci', '12eng'
  name text not null,
  grade_level int not null check (grade_level in (11, 12)),
  stream text not null,
  is_active boolean default true,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

create table class_subjects (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  class_id text references classes(id) on delete cascade not null,
  subject_code text not null,
  subject_name text not null,
  weekly_quota int default 2,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 5. STUDENTS & ANNUAL ENROLLMENTS
create table students (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  admission_no text unique,
  registration_no text unique,
  full_name text not null,
  gender text check (gender in ('M', 'F', 'O')),
  is_active boolean default true,
  archived_at timestamp with time zone,
  archive_reason text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

create table student_enrollments (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  academic_year_id text references academic_years(id) on delete cascade not null,
  class_id text references classes(id) on delete cascade not null,
  student_id uuid references students(id) on delete cascade not null,
  roll_number int not null,
  section text not null default 'A',
  status text not null default 'active' check (status in ('active', 'transferred', 'graduated', 'archived', 'completed')),
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now(),
  unique (academic_year_id, class_id, roll_number),
  unique (academic_year_id, class_id, student_id)
);

-- 6. WORKSTATIONS & CAD FLOOR ELEMENTS
create table workstations (
  id text primary key, -- e.g. 'PC-01'
  lab_id text references labs(id) on delete cascade not null,
  label text not null,
  pos_x float not null default 0,
  pos_y float not null default 0,
  device_type text not null default 'pc',
  row_label text,
  is_active boolean default true,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

create table floor_elements (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  lab_id text references labs(id) on delete cascade not null,
  element_type text not null, -- 'door', 'window', 'pillar', 'board', 'podium', 'bench'
  label text,
  pos_x float not null default 0,
  pos_y float not null default 0,
  width float not null default 80,
  height float not null default 40,
  rotation float not null default 0
);

create table workstation_seat_plans (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  lab_id text references labs(id) on delete cascade not null,
  academic_year_id text references academic_years(id) on delete cascade not null,
  class_id text references classes(id) on delete cascade not null,
  workstation_id text references workstations(id) on delete cascade not null,
  enrollment_id uuid references student_enrollments(id) on delete cascade not null,
  notes text,
  assigned_by uuid references profiles(id),
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now(),
  unique (lab_id, academic_year_id, class_id, workstation_id),
  unique (lab_id, academic_year_id, class_id, enrollment_id)
);

create table workstation_issues (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  workstation_id text references workstations(id) on delete cascade not null,
  reported_by uuid references profiles(id),
  title text not null,
  description text,
  severity text not null check (severity in ('low', 'medium', 'high', 'critical')),
  status text not null default 'open' check (status in ('open', 'in_progress', 'resolved')),
  resolved_at timestamp with time zone,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 7. MASTER ROUTINES & TIMETABLE
create table schedules (
  id text primary key,
  day_of_week int not null, -- 0=Sunday to 5=Friday
  time_slot text not null,
  slot_id text not null,
  span int default 1,
  lab_id text references labs(id) on delete cascade not null,
  teacher_id uuid references profiles(id) on delete set null,
  subject_code text not null,
  subject_title text not null,
  class_grade text not null,
  default_students int default 36,
  status text default 'active',
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 8. PRACTICAL LOG ENTRIES (Academic Session Records)
create table practical_logs (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  schedule_id text references schedules(id) on delete set null,
  lab_id text references labs(id) on delete cascade not null,
  teacher_id uuid references profiles(id) on delete set null,
  date text not null, -- YYYY-MM-DD
  period_label text,
  subject_name text not null,
  batch_group text,
  practical_title text,
  topic_learned text,
  total_students int not null default 0,
  present_students int not null default 0,
  absent_students int not null default 0,
  absent_rolls int[] default '{}',
  status session_status default 'completed',
  skip_reason text,
  remarks text,
  logged_by uuid references profiles(id),
  academic_year_id text references academic_years(id),
  class_subject_id uuid references class_subjects(id),
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 9. PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE PLANS & SERVICE LOGS
create table maintenance_plans (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  title text not null,
  description text,
  lab_id text references labs(id) on delete cascade not null,
  cadence maintenance_cadence not null default 'monthly',
  checklist text[] default '{}',
  affected_machines text[] default '{}',
  category text not null default 'hardware',
  is_active boolean default true,
  created_by uuid references profiles(id),
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

create table maintenance_logs (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  plan_id uuid references maintenance_plans(id) on delete set null,
  lab_id text references labs(id) on delete cascade not null,
  performed_by uuid references profiles(id) on delete set null,
  performed_at timestamp with time zone default now(),
  asset_identifier text,
  work_performed text,
  observations text,
  next_recommended_date text,
  status text not null default 'completed',
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 10. EQUIPMENT BREAKAGE & INCIDENT REGISTER
create table lab_incidents (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  title text not null,
  lab_id text references labs(id) on delete cascade not null,
  reported_by uuid references profiles(id) on delete set null,
  equipment_name text not null,
  incident_type text not null,
  severity incident_severity default 'minor',
  status incident_status default 'reported',
  escalated_to_hod boolean default false,
  resolution_notes text,
  resolved_at timestamp with time zone,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);

-- 11. IMMUTABLE AUDIT LEDGER
create table audit_ledger (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  entity_type text not null,
  entity_id text not null,
  action text not null,
  actor_id uuid references profiles(id),
  before_state jsonb,
  after_state jsonb,
  metadata jsonb default '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default now()
);
```

---

## 4. Core Feature Specifications & Module Breakdown

### Module 1: Authentication, Access Approvals & Security Shell
- **Email/Password & OTP Flow**: Supabase Auth client/server integration (`@supabase/ssr`).
- **Account Approval Pipeline**: New accounts start in `pending` approval status. Super Admins approve or reject registrations from the Admin Console.
- **Top Navigation & Global Command Palette**:
  - Prominent search pill (`Search sessions, rooms, faculty... Ctrl+K` / `⌘K`).
  - Hydration-safe state synchronization powered by React 19's `useSyncExternalStore`.
  - Live clock indicator rendering Nepal Standard Time (NPT) with active period tracking.
- **User Profile Menu**: Renders role badge, assigned facility scope, theme toggle, and secure sign-out.

### Module 2: Live Operational Command Center (`/`)
- **Live Session Cockpit**:
  - Two-state dynamic dispatcher (Active Session Running vs. Standby / Next Upcoming).
  - Concentric radar pulse pip (`animate-ping`) for real-time in-session telemetry.
  - Multi-lab horizontal switcher for admins and coordinators to inspect concurrent sessions across rooms.
  - 1-click **Log Attendance** and **Skip Session** triggers.
- **High-Density KPI Row (Zero Card-in-Card Nesting)**:
  - 3 standalone `.glass-card` elements in a `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3 gap-2.5 sm:gap-3` at ~76px total height.
  - Row 1: Tinted icon badge + title (left) | status pill (right).
  - Row 2: Bold metric (`text-xl font-extrabold font-heading`) on left | micro-context / progress bar on right.
- **Quick Operations Strip**:
  - Synchronized ~76px height in right column (`Print Report` + `New Log` + `Daily Sheet ↗`).
- **Three-Tier Semantic Attendance System**:
  - `>= 85%`: Success (Emerald text + emerald badge `Optimal`)
  - `75% - 84%`: Nominal (Neutral slate text + neutral badge `Normal` — zero false warning)
  - `< 75%`: Danger (Rose text + rose badge `Low Rate`)
  - `0%` / Pending: Neutral dash `—` + neutral badge `Awaiting`

### Module 3: Interactive CAD Floor Plan & Workstation Cockpit (`/computer-lab`)
- **CAD Pan/Zoom Interactive Viewport**:
  - Smooth clamping ($0.5\times$ to $1.6\times$) with cursor-centered focal scaling.
  - Multi-touch pinch zoom, middle-click and `Space + Drag` panning, and focus auto-centering.
- **Floating HUD Canvas Controls**:
  - Zoom in/out, 1:1 reset, fit-to-screen, pan mode toggle, radar minimap toggle. Strictly zero literal `+` in labels.
- **Collapsible Minimap Radar**:
  - Real-time 34-node room preview with attendance/status micro-dots and interactive draggable/clickable bounding viewport box.
- **Living LCD Workstation Nodes**:
  - Chamfered extruded bezels (`inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.08)`), power status LEDs, glowing roll-call rings, and tactile spring click response (`active:scale-95`).
- **High-Speed Roll-Call Accelerators**:
  - Jump-to-Roll input with instant viewport pan & focal halo beacon.
  - "Mark All Present", "Invert Attendance", and live 3-tier attendance indicator.
- **Quick Station Popover**:
  - Floating 1-tap popover for attendance toggle, Tier 2 seat partner swap, and direct fault report ticket creation.
- **Official A4 Wall Seating Chart (`/print/seating-chart`)**:
  - Laminated printable room chart grouped by rows A–D with teacher podium.

### Module 4: Dual Calendar & Nepali Date Engine
- **Bilingual Gregorian (AD) & Bikram Sambat (BS)**:
  - Integrated Nepali calendar converter (`nepali-date-converter`, `lib/nepali-calendar.ts`).
  - Dual Calendar Picker component (`components/admin/dual-calendar-picker.tsx`) showing simultaneous BS year/month/day and AD equivalent.
- **Academic Holiday & Recess Detection**:
  - Auto-identifies gazetted national and institutional holidays.
  - Whole-day suspension banners automatically replace routine grids on recess dates.

### Module 5: Weekly Routine & Timetable Grid (`/schedules`)
- **Sunday–Friday Academic Week Schedule**:
  - Full support for standard Nepali school/college 6-day academic operating cycle.
- **Live "Now" Timeline Beacon**:
  - Highlights ongoing period slot with a pulsating `LIVE` badge and ambient column tint.
- **2-Line Slot Typography Hierarchy**:
  - Line 1: Subject Code & Class Grade/Batch in bold.
  - Line 2: Teacher Name and Micro-Time Slot Badge (zero horizontal truncation).
- **Consecutive Period Merging**:
  - Seamless consolidation of two continuous periods into a single extended practical block.

### Module 6: Triple-Collision Defense Engine (`lib/scheduling/conflict-engine.ts`)
- Pre-flight validation executed before creating schedules or ad-hoc practical logs.
- Guarding 3 critical conflict dimensions:
  1. **Room Collision**: Prevents double-booking the same lab at overlapping times on the same day.
  2. **Faculty Collision**: Prevents scheduling the same instructor in multiple rooms at the same time.
  3. **Student Cohort Collision**: Prevents double-booking a class/batch across concurrent practicals.

### Module 7: Canonical Institutional Reporting & Operational Intelligence (`/analytics`)
- **Zero Shadow Databases**: All metrics derived directly on-the-fly from live PostgreSQL operational tables.
- **NEB 75% Board Exam Practical Compliance**:
  - Class-wise student practical attendance tally, total session hours, present hours, percentage rate, and compliance flag (`Eligible` vs. `At Risk`).
- **Syllabus Practical Quota & Skipped Sessions**:
  - Track term syllabus experiment quotas per subject, completed sessions, and categorize reasons for skipped lab slots.
- **Faculty Practical Operations & Dual Sign-Off Audit**:
  - Teacher session logging volume, dual sign-off verification rate by Lab In-Charge, and pending verification backlog.
- **Laboratory Room Occupancy Index**:
  - Standard 36-period academic weekly capacity, booked periods, occupancy percentage, and total student footfall.
- **Workstation Reliability & MTTR Hotspots**:
  - Workstation uptime %, Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR in hours), and repeat fault hotspots.
- **Workstation Technical Biography Drawer**:
  - Interactive slide-out lifecycle timeline showing historical faults, preventive maintenance services, and past student seating history for any PC.

### Module 8: Multi-Year Academic Lifecycle & Cohort Promotion
- **Academic Year Management**: Multi-cycle support (`2082/83`, `2083/84`) with active operational cycle switching.
- **Atomic Cohort Promotion (`promoteCohortAction`)**:
  - Mass promotion from Grade 11 to Grade 12.
  - Exception handling for repeaters (retained in same grade) and transfers/dropouts (archived).
  - Enforced check constraint: `status IN ('active', 'transferred', 'graduated', 'archived', 'completed')`.

### Module 9: Preventive Maintenance Workbench (`/maintenance`)
- **2-Tab Architecture**:
  - **Tab 1: Routine Tasks & Schedules**: Active maintenance routines, cadence, last serviced date & technician, next due status badges (`Overdue`, `Due Today`, `Scheduled`), and 1-click **Record Service** or **Postpone**.
  - **Tab 2: Certified Service History & Logbook**: Searchable historical logbook with machine checklists, observations, and printable log sheet.
- **Interactive 40-Workstation Matrix (`WorkstationMatrixSelector`)**:
  - Visual grid of PC desks (`PC-01` to `PC-40`).
  - 3-State cycling on desk click: Pending &rarr; Cleaned & Serviced &rarr; Flagged Faulty.
  - Batch Action Toolbar: `Select All`, `Invert`, `Flag Faults`, `Reset`.
- **Institutional Digital Sign-Off Certificate Stamp**:
  - Institutional seal stamp rendered on maintenance log completion.
- **Zero Pricing Clutter**: Strictly focused on technical compliance (cleaning, thermal paste, BIOS, OS updates, cable routing, glassware safety) without budgetary noise.

### Module 10: Equipment Breakage & Incident Register (`/incidents` & `/records/incidents`)
- **Breakage Intake**: Equipment name, damage type, severity (`minor`, `moderate`, `major_critical`), and description notes.
- **HOD Escalation Trigger**: High-severity incidents automatically flag for Department Head / Coordinator intervention.
- **Settlement & Repair Drawer**: Lab In-Charge records repairs, replacements, student compensation status, or decommissioning.

### Module 11: Multi-Format Board Exports & Real-Time Reminders
- **ExcelJS Export Engine (`lib/exports/xlsx.ts`)**:
  - Official NEB Practical Attendance & Board Exam Compliance Register with institutional header styling, alternating row striping, auto-width columns, and 3-tier signature blocks ("Subject Teacher", "Lab In-Charge", "HOD / Principal").
- **CSV Dataset Export (`lib/exports/csv.ts`)**: Clean raw comma-separated values for school data systems.
- **Real-Time Reminders Queue (`getInstitutionalReminders`)**:
  - Derived alert notifications for critical workstation faults, overdue preventive maintenance, and unverified practical sessions.

### Module 12: High-Fidelity A4 Landscape Print Engine (`/print/*`)
- **Available Print Sheets**:
  - `/print/daily-log`: Daily institutional laboratory sign-off register.
  - `/print/records`: Filtered historical practical session register.
  - `/print/incidents`: Institutional equipment damage and hazard register.
  - `/print/maintenance`: Technical maintenance logbook and servicing certificate.
  - `/print/seating-chart`: Laminated physical room seating chart.
- **Print Shield Architecture**: `@media print` CSS rules automatically strip sidebars, command palettes, theme toggles, and backgrounds, enforcing a pure white background with crisp black typography and dual signature blocks.

### Module 13: Institutional Admin Console & Safety Lock (`/admin`)
- **Tab 1: User Access & Approvals**: Manage registrations, assign roles, reset credentials.
- **Tab 2: Master Timetable Routine Manager**: Edit weekly schedule periods, map subject codes to faculty.
- **Tab 3: Maintenance Routines Manager**: Edit checklists, toggle active/paused routines, and 1-click install recommended SOP presets.
- **Tab 4: Institution Settings**: Configure institution name, shift structures, and academic terms.
- **Precaution Active Safety Switch**: A mandatory toggle guard that prevents accidental edits or deletions in administrative tools.

## 5. Visual Design System & Interaction Standards

### Color Tokens & Palette Hierarchy
- **Dark Theme (Deep Obsidian & Midnight Slate)**:
  - Canvas: `#0B0F19`
  - Surface-1: `#101726`
  - Surface-2: `#151E32`
  - Surface-3: `#1A253D`
  - Hairline Borders: `border-white/[0.08]`
  - Milled Chamfer Highlight: `inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06)`

  - Canvas: `#F8FAFC`
  - Surface: `#FFFFFF`
  - Hairline Borders: `border-zinc-200/80`

  - Heading: `Plus Jakarta Sans` (`font-heading`)
  - Body & UI: `Inter` (`font-sans`)
  - Bilingual Devanagari Fallback: `Noto Sans Devanagari` (`--font-devanagari`)
  - Monospace / Numerics: `JetBrains Mono` (`font-mono`) with global `tabular-nums`
- **Tactile Physics**:
  - Buttons compress `2–3%` on click (`active:scale-[0.97]` with `motion-reduce:active:scale-100`).
  - Cards elevate on hover (`hover:-translate-y-0.5 hover:shadow-xs transition-all duration-150 ease-out`).

## 6. Critical Developer Guardrails & Invariants

1. **NO Literal `+` in Button Labels**: Always pair icons with natural text (`<Plus className="h-4 w-4" /> <span>Record Service</span>`), never `<span>+ Record Service</span>`.
2. **Standardized Academic Terminology**:
   - Use **"Attendance"** — never "Turnout".
   - Use **"Timetable"** or **"Schedule Grid"** — never "Matrix".
   - Use **"Logbook"** — never "Ledger".
   - Use **"Equipment Breakage"** — never "Apparatus Breakage".
3. **Safety Lock**: The Super Admin safety switch is named **"Precaution Active"**; retain this label and functionality.
4. **Zero Pricing/Cost Clutter**: Maintenance logs and plans track technical compliance only. No financial fields.
5. **Zero Department Regressions**: Never re-introduce department strings to profiles or tables. Use Role Badges and Facility Scopes.
6. **Zero Shadow Databases**: All analytics and reports must query canonical PostgreSQL tables directly.
7. **Triple-Collision Validation**: Every schedule slot and live booking must pass Room, Faculty, and Cohort collision checks.
8. **Strict TypeScript Standards**: All code must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` with **0 errors**.
9. **Next.js `'use server'` Rules**: Server action files must only export async functions. Domain constants, types, and synchronous validators belong in `lib/`.
10. **Derived Workstation Status**: Workstation operational state is derived from `workstation_issues`, not a static column.
